recipes.name: Butternut Squash Risotto
ingredients_raw: salt and ground black pepper to taste

steps.text: Place squash into a steamer basket in a saucepan; fill with water to just below the bottom of the basket. Cover, bring to a boil, and steam squash until tender, 10 to 15 minutes. Drain; use a fork to mash squash in a bowl.

Melt butter in a saucepan over medium-high heat. Add onion; cook and stir for 2 minutes until onion begins to soften, then stir in rice. Continue cooking and stirring until rice is glossy and the onion begins to brown on the edges, about 5 minutes more.
Pour in white wine; cook, stirring constantly, until it has evaporated. Stir in mashed squash and 1/3 of the hot chicken stock; reduce heat to medium.

Cook and stir until chicken stock has been absorbed into rice, 5 to 7 minutes. Add 1/2 of the remaining chicken stock, and continue stirring until it has been absorbed. Finally, pour in remaining stock, and continue stirring until the risotto is creamy.
Stir in Parmesan cheese and season with salt and pepper.

raw_recipe.headline: Butternut Squash Risotto
raw_recipe.description: This creamy butternut squash risotto is an easy, comforting risotto to make for those who love the naturally sweet flavor of tender butternut squash.

review.reviewBody: Loved this! So delicious and flavorful, especially once the parmesan has been added. Peeling and chopping butternut squash is a pain. Here's my suggestion - simply cut the squash in half and remove the seeds with a spoon. Then, place (peel down) on a baking sheet and bake at 400 for 40-45 min, or until the squash is tender. Then, just scoop out the squash and voila! easy puree!

The liquid measurement was, indeed, totally off. I want to say I used no more than 3 - 3.5 cups in all. The flavor is good, especially after the addition of the parmesan. I used veggie broth in place of chicken, and added quite a bit of black pepper. Per another user's suggestion, I cut the squash in half, brushed with olive oil and roasted at 400 degrees, face down, for about an hour, then simply scooped out the squash. I pureed it with 1 cup of broth in a blender to get it super silky smooth. I would make this again!

This was a good start towards a great recipe. I made a few minor modifications to suit my taste. I absolutely LOVE the combination of butternut squash and sage so adding that was a given. I used shallots in liu of onions just for that hint of garlic and lastly, but I think most importantly since I’ve tried it both ways, after cubing my squash, I roasted it in the oven at 350 for about 40 (until completely tender and Carmalized on the edges) then mashed them prior to adding them to the rice mixture. The added depth of flavor is so much more rich without being overpowering.

Loved this recipe. Like many others, I roasted the squash for about an hour, and then pureed it with a pinch of cinnamon and a cup of broth. I added garlic and diced mushrooms, cooking them with the onions in the butter. I also used 1/3 of a cup of parmesan cheese, and only used 3 cups of broth (inclusive of the cup used for the puree). I mixed in the puree closer to the end, and seasoned only with a bit of pepper after the cheese was fully blended in. It worked out perfectly. Tasted delicious. Will definitely make this again.

Steamed small butternut squash cubes in microwave for 3 minutes to soften. Then sauteed squash in olive oil with minced garlic, salt, pepper and paprika. Did not mash squash. Reduced chicken stock to 3 1/2 cups and followed the recipe for the rest of the preparation. The result was a very flavorful side dish because of garlic and paprika. Paired well with a walnut-crusted baked tilapia.

This recipe is a good base, but with a few tweaks it can be changed from bland to delicious! Like others have said I cut and placed the butternut squash in the oven for an hour at 400 which made it so much easier to mash. However, next time I will probably get a can or try some other method in order to make this quicker. Added in some cinnamon, nutmeg, and garlic (with the onions) in order to give it some flavor and it tasted amazing! I actually did use quite a bit of chicken stock (~4 cups) in order to make the arborio rice become soft and make the dish creamier so I would suggest placing the stock cup by cup and add more if you feel like it is needed. Also, I added the butternut squash after the first several cups of stock in order to make sure the rice absorbed the liquid properly. Perfect dish for fall and if these extra ingredients are added, the dish becomes both sweet and savory.

Freaking delicious! Made as per recipe except veggi broth instead of chicken broth.. I was skeptacle about the amount of liquid, but followed the recipe and it was spot on fantastic!!! Will make this a monthly staple in my kitchen; thanks!!!

For the squash, I cut in quarters, removed seeds, microwaved for 8 mins, scooped out the cooked squash, mashed with a fork! Easy, no mess, and no peeling necsssary!

Delicious base recipe. Added 2 oz pancetta and substituted shallots for onions. Waited to add squash until risotto was cooked, because I like to taste the squash. Garlic would probably be a good addition too.
I used all the bouillon, but cut back around 1 cup of water. This is excellent! I peeled and steamed the squash in the microwave before preparing the rest of the dish. I am glad that I did this.

I added 3 cloves of garlic and rosemary. I also cubed the butternut squash instead of mashing it, then roasted the squash for 45 mins in a 400 degree oven. It was delicious! Others mentioned they only used 2-3 cups of chicken stock. I definitely don’t recommend that. I needed all 5 cups and it turned out perfectly creamy.

The dish is excellent and I recommend it alongside Mary's Meatloaf (an Allrecipes fav of mine), sauteed fresh spinach, homemade french bread, and a green salad - a beautiful Sunday afternoon meal that fed the body and the soul. I chose to roast my butternut squash in the oven (instead of steaming it as the recipe directs). I cut the squash in half (length-wise), brushed the flesh with olive oil, salt and pepper, some high quality lightly dried sage, and roasted it (flesh up) until it was completely cooked. I scooped the squash out with a fork and added it to the risotto as it was cooking. It's dishes like this risotto that make fall such a delicious, magical time of year.
Absolutely yummy. My guests loved it too and asked for it at lunch the next day.

I made this recipe without any changes or additions. The recipe was easy to follow and the result was excellent. I had this as a main course and served a couple of vegetables with it. The flavor was spot on and I would definitely make this again.

Yes, I too roast the butternut squash in the convection oven to soften it before ever touching it with a knife. Or! I really cheat and buy frozen bags of butternut squash. Also yes to using a bit less broth although it IS risotto which is a goopier version of rice. Still I didn't care for this. I Made it the way the recipe called for, I thought it was bland so I began doctoring.. still couldnt make it tatste better than my buttery mushroom risotto so That's what I'm sticking with and this is coming out of my saves.
Very flavourful! But way too much broth. I used about 3 cups instead of the recommended 5 cups. The consistency was perfect.

Maybe it was just too healthy tasting...It would work well for a side dish. We felt like it needed something more, I added more cheese but still didn't satisfy. It seemed to make too much for one meal, there are three of us.

I added a little salt and fresh grated nutmeg to the mashed squash before adding it to the rice. Glad I did! I tasted a little bit each time I added broth and ended up adding a pinch of salt each time and then about a half teaspoon of poultry seasoning and a few cracks of fresh peppper during the last addition of chicken stock. Definitely will make this way again!
My husband and I both loved this recipe. It is easy to follow and tasted great!
My whole family loved it! Like others, I roasted the squash. First, I made sage butter, then followed the recipe. Like others, only used 2 cups water. Delicious!
Good recipe, but 4 cups of hot stock per 1 cup of arborio rice is about right. Makes for a thicker (less runny) risotto.
